```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_small <- simulate_bdat602(n = 10000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1 — Full preprocessing pipeline

```{r task1}
library(recipes)

pp_rec <- recipe(claim_amount ~ ., data = health_small) |>
  step_impute_median(bmi, income) |>
  step_dummy(sex, region, one_hot = FALSE) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

pp_prep          <- prep(pp_rec, training = health_small)
health_processed <- bake(pp_prep, new_data = health_small)

cat("NAs in bmi:   ", sum(is.na(health_processed$bmi)),    "\n")
cat("NAs in income:", sum(is.na(health_processed$income)),  "\n")
cat("Mean of bmi:  ", round(mean(health_processed$bmi), 4), "\n")
```

`bmi` and `income` have 0 NAs. The mean of scaled `bmi` is approximately 0 and the SD is approximately 1.

## Task 2 — Column count before and after step_nzv

```{r task2}
cat("Columns without nzv:", ncol(health_processed), "\n")

pp_rec2 <- recipe(claim_amount ~ ., data = health_small) |>
  step_impute_median(bmi, income) |>
  step_dummy(sex, region, one_hot = FALSE) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_nzv(all_predictors())

pp_prep2  <- prep(pp_rec2, training = health_small)
health_p2 <- bake(pp_prep2, new_data = health_small)

cat("Columns with nzv:   ", ncol(health_p2), "\n")
```

`step_nzv()` typically removes one or two near-constant dummy columns (e.g. rare categories that appear in fewer than 10% of rows after encoding). The exact columns depend on the random seed.
